understanding: The OKO live service must alert a user in Telegram, but ONLY for VLM-described events (human/animal → gemini description), formatted as «👁 ОКО: <описание>», and must work on a webcam out-of-the-box. Reading the code reveals the contract is partly out of sync with reality: (a) the real interface is the abstract `Reporter` in src/oko/live/reporters.py (report(self, payload: BridgeOutput)), not 'EventReporter'; (b) a `TelegramReporter` ALREADY exists there but is richer (photo/video, verbose `_format`) and is gated on `payload.should_alert`, not on VLM description; (c) the secrets-loading pattern already exists in src/oko/providers/gemini_vlm.py via `_load_gemini_api_key_from_secrets()` reading ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json; (d) the current Settings default config_path is 'configs/fake-live.yaml' (not example.yaml), and `build_reporter_from_env` reads OKO_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID/OKO_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, while the task wants OKO_TG_CHAT + token-from-secrets. So this is a focused EXTENSION/RECONCILIATION of existing code plus a default flip, not a greenfield build.
summary: Extend the existing TelegramReporter with an additive 'VLM-only OKO-alert' mode (gate on non-empty payload.description, emit «👁 ОКО: <описание>»), add a `_load_telegram_bot_token_from_secrets()` helper mirroring the gemini one, wire it through the service's existing reporter factory (`build_reporter_from_env`) so a TelegramReporter is appended only when OKO_TG_CHAT is set, and flip Settings.config_path default to configs/live-webcam.yaml. Keep all existing behavior/tests intact; add focused tests with injected transport. Disabled by default (no chat_id ⇒ not added).

decision_atoms.statement: Interpret 'EventReporter' as the existing abstract `Reporter` (src/oko/live/reporters.py) and implement against its `report(self, payload: BridgeOutput) -> None`; optionally add `EventReporter = Reporter` as an alias for contract fidelity.
decision_atoms.reason: There is no `EventReporter` class in the repo; `Reporter` is the established ABC that all reporters and the pipeline worker already use. Building against it satisfies the intent without forking the interface.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slight literal mismatch with the contract's wording; the optional alias resolves it but adds a name that isn't otherwise used.

decision_atoms.statement: Add the behavior to the EXISTING TelegramReporter via an additive `vlm_only`/`alert_format='oko'` flag (default off) rather than creating a second class; in that mode send iff `payload.description` is non-empty and post text `f'👁 ОКО: {payload.description}'`.
decision_atoms.reason: A TelegramReporter already exists with the required transport injection (`_http_post`) and retry logic; reusing it avoids duplication. Making the new gate/format opt-in preserves the ~20 existing should_alert-based tests (e.g. test at line 587 sends on should_alert with empty description).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The class grows another mode/branch instead of being split into single-responsibility reporters; risk of mode confusion, mitigated by clear defaults and the service only enabling the new mode.

decision_atoms.statement: Use non-empty `BridgeOutput.description` (the gemini VLM text) as the discriminator for 'VLM event'; object-only events keep the default `description=''` and are not sent.
decision_atoms.reason: `description` is the only field carrying the gemini human/animal narrative; it is empty for object-only/non-VLM events. This needs no new domain field and directly satisfies the 'NOT object-events' success test.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Couples alert gating to a string being populated upstream; if a non-VLM path ever sets description, it would leak an alert. Low likelihood given current pipeline.

decision_atoms.statement: Add `_load_telegram_bot_token_from_secrets()` reading field `telegramBotToken` from ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json, mirroring `_load_gemini_api_key_from_secrets()` (fail-soft: return None on missing file / bad JSON).
decision_atoms.reason: Reuses an established, tested pattern in the same codebase, keeping secrets handling consistent and offline-safe.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Token source differs from the existing OKO_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN env path, creating two token sources; documented precedence (secrets for the OKO_TG_CHAT path) keeps it predictable.

decision_atoms.statement: Wire enablement through the service's existing reporter factory `build_reporter_from_env()` (which service.py already injects as `_reporter_factory`): when OKO_TG_CHAT is set AND a token resolves, append a vlm_only «👁 ОКО:» TelegramReporter; otherwise add nothing.
decision_atoms.reason: service.py constructs its reporter via this factory, so extending it satisfies 'service adds TelegramReporter when OKO_TG_CHAT is set' while keeping reporter logic in reporters.py. OFF-by-default falls out naturally (no chat_id ⇒ not appended).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Slightly looser than a literal edit in service.py; if a reviewer expects the branch physically in service.py, note this is the same wiring path. Avoid double-sending with the legacy telegram env reporter by not enabling both for the same chat.

decision_atoms.statement: Change Settings.config_path default from 'configs/fake-live.yaml' to 'configs/live-webcam.yaml' and update the corresponding service test assertion.
decision_atoms.reason: Makes the service run on a webcam out-of-the-box per the task; live-webcam.yaml already exists. The default is read by Settings.from_env and is trivially testable (Settings().config_path).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: live-webcam requires a real camera at runtime (readiness may block on machines without one); tests inject factories so they stay green, but a bare `python -m service` on a headless box now fails readiness instead of running the fake source.

decision_atoms.statement: Test exclusively through the injected `_http_post` transport, asserting (1) a VLM event posts to api.telegram.org with body text «👁 ОКО: <описание>» and the configured chat_id, and (2) an object-only event (description='') performs zero posts; plus a unit test that Settings default config_path == 'configs/live-webcam.yaml'.
decision_atoms.reason: Mirrors the existing test_reporters.py convention (fake_post capturing urllib Request, `_sample_output(...)`), keeps tests offline and deterministic, and maps 1:1 to the success_tests.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Tests the transport boundary, not real Telegram delivery; the real end-to-end success test ('actually sends on webcam') stays manual/out of CI.

assumptions: 'EventReporter' in the contract refers to the existing abstract `Reporter` class; no separate EventReporter is required.
Human/animal VLM events are exactly those where BridgeOutput.description (gemini text) is non-empty; object-only events leave description=''.
~/.bridge-private/secrets.json contains a `telegramBotToken` string field, consistent with the existing telegramBotToken/secrets references found in the repo.
configs/live-webcam.yaml is a valid, present config and is the intended out-of-the-box webcam profile.
pytest is the test runner and new tests belong in tests/ following test_reporters.py / test_service.py conventions.
Keeping the legacy OKO_TELEGRAM_* env path working alongside the new OKO_TG_CHAT path is acceptable, with OKO_TG_CHAT driving the new vlm_only «👁 ОКО:» alert.
Sending a plain sendMessage text (not photo/video) is sufficient for the minimal acceptance; HTTP body is UTF-8 encoded so emoji/Cyrillic round-trip.

risks.risk: Re-gating the existing TelegramReporter on description (instead of should_alert) would break the ~20 existing should_alert-based reporter tests.
risks.mitigation: Make the new gate/format an opt-in mode (default off). Default construction keeps should_alert behavior; only the OKO_TG_CHAT service path enables vlm_only. Run full pytest to confirm no regressions.

risks.risk: Flipping the default config_path to live-webcam.yaml can break service tests asserting the old default and can fail live readiness on machines without a camera.
risks.mitigation: Update the service test's expected default; tests inject config/readiness factories so they stay hermetic. Document that headless runs need OKO_CONFIG_PATH override or a camera; keep fake-live available via env.

risks.risk: Two telegram env paths (OKO_TG_CHAT+secrets vs OKO_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID+env token) could double-send or confuse operators.
risks.mitigation: Define precedence and avoid registering two telegram reporters for the same chat; document OKO_TG_CHAT as the supported alert toggle. Optionally suppress the legacy path when OKO_TG_CHAT is set.

risks.risk: Secrets file absent in CI ⇒ token None ⇒ reporter silently not added, which could mask a wiring bug or cause a false 'works' impression.
risks.mitigation: Offline tests inject bot_token/chat_id directly (never depend on the real secrets file). The factory logs when OKO_TG_CHAT is set but no token resolves, so misconfiguration is visible.

risks.risk: Contract 'EventReporter' naming mismatch leads a reviewer to expect a different base class or a renamed interface.
risks.mitigation: State the interpretation explicitly and optionally export `EventReporter = Reporter`; do not rename the established ABC, which the pipeline worker depends on.

risks.risk: Emoji/Cyrillic mis-encoding garbles the «👁 ОКО:» message.
risks.mitigation: Encode the JSON body with .encode('utf-8') (as existing code does) and assert the exact decoded string in the test.

minimal_version: 1) In src/oko/live/reporters.py add an opt-in mode to TelegramReporter (e.g. ctor flag `vlm_only=False`, `alert_format` default unchanged): when enabled, `report` returns early unless `payload.description.strip()` is truthy, and posts a sendMessage JSON body {chat_id, text: f'👁 ОКО: {payload.description}'} via the injected `_http_post`. 2) Add `_load_telegram_bot_token_from_secrets()` mirroring the gemini secrets loader, reading `telegramBotToken`. 3) Extend `build_reporter_from_env()`: if OKO_TG_CHAT is set and a token resolves (secrets), append a vlm_only TelegramReporter; else add nothing (OFF by default). 4) In service.py change Settings.config_path default to 'configs/live-webcam.yaml'. 5) Tests: with injected transport, a VLM event (description set) posts «👁 ОКО: <описание>» to the correct chat_id, an object-only event posts nothing, and Settings().config_path == 'configs/live-webcam.yaml'; update any existing default-config assertion. pytest green.
advanced_version: Beyond the minimal: use «👁 ОКО: <описание>» as the caption when a keyframe/incident video is present so the user gets image/clip alerts; add config-file driven chat_id and an optional bot-token override (ReporterConfig.telegram_alert_format / telegram_chat_id_source) so YAML can enable it without env; suppress/dedupe against the legacy OKO_TELEGRAM_* reporter to prevent double alerts; export `EventReporter = Reporter` for contract fidelity; document OKO_TG_CHAT in configs/live-webcam.yaml and README; add an integration-style test driving a fake webcam frame through LivePipelineWorker to assert an alert is emitted end-to-end with the reporter factory; and structured logging of 'telegram_alert_sent' for observability.
